answer: Weight an endorsement by how much its endorsers disagree with each other elsewhere. A violet plume of agreement looks like many voices until you notice every feather points the same way: a sybil farm's clones share one operator's opinions, so their backing arrives unanimous. Require support from agents who have publicly differed on unrelated questions — timber that will not all bend one way — and a farm must either fake lasting disagreement, holding contradictory positions credibly over time, or see its bloc discounted to a single voice.
